observations: The full traversal scene has a clear departure, landing ledge and one airborne Riven; the small fox gives the destination an inhabited purpose.
The cool city has strong depth, but the figure and fox become dark and small on a phone. The ribbons suggest movement without fully explaining the seam rule.
Solene, her single axe and the descent into a buried hall remain recognizable in a new discovery pose. The warm treatment supplies the clearest lighting contrast in the scene set.
The golden fault reads differently from the predominantly cyan vocabulary. This is a provisional regional/lighting variation, not an approved world rule.

Vale and Iria remain separate grounded adults with one weapon each, a clear channel between them, and a small heron above. The brush treatment preserves the confrontation's readable black-and-white masses.
Iria's forearm guard remains on the empty-hand side, matching C03's actual image rather than its written intention. The alternate route is suggested, not established geography.

The forest bridge, braced fighter and heavy creature make an appealing encounter, but the intended shoulder stop is not clearly shown: the blade crosses the head region and the bright contact sits near its root.
The repair lowered the head but reduced and simplified the signature spearhead without resolving the contact. The primary remains displayed; both attempts are in History.
The repair restores Dax's anatomical right gauntlet and keeps the standing power event, both planted boots, divided slab and deep hall readable.
This is a partial correction: a bright electric gap still makes exact knuckle-to-stone contact uncertain. Do not treat the image as a solved physical action diagram.
The repair restores Senn beside Riven while retaining their complete weapons and the enormous long-necked Regent among inhabited city blocks.
The scene is a strong scale/atmosphere study. The figures face mostly away, so Senn's face and front armor remain weak continuity evidence, especially on a phone.
Riven's silver swept-back hair, dark petrol tailoring and relaxed face give him a distinct recurring identity; the full saber is framed.
The dark full figure and narrow ledge are harder to read on a phone. The pose does not independently demonstrate safe footing or his movement ability.
Senn has a confident face, muscular silhouette and two clear shaft grips.
Her spearhead exits the right edge, and its inherited enclosed aperture differs from the brief's central notch. Full weapon construction is clearer in G02; the framing defect remains.
Iria's ponytail, focused face and oxblood jacket distinguish her from the other adults, with one framed pistol.
The silver guard is on her empty left arm rather than the specified weapon side; the body is longer and slimmer than the compact brief. Linked images also lose some equipment details.
The repair restores the powered gauntlet to Dax's anatomical right arm and replaces the active wall punch with a clearer ready guard.
His bearded face, build and armor remain recognizable in the linked actions. Metallic facets and small blue effects still add detail beyond a quiet character sheet.
Solene's grin, curls and warm outlined treatment create a lively combat identity. Both hands hold separated shaft grips and the single axe head remains clear.
The large sun arc and ruin background exceed the intended quiet character presentation. The linked discovery scene is a useful check on her appeal without the large effect.
Vale's broad greatsword, two-handed hold, full stance and graphic white/black silhouette are readable.
The brush treatment differs substantially from Nightglass, intentionally as a comparison. Some face and clothing detail is more modeled than the original graphic anchor.
The complete dark-and-cyan saber has a recognizable guard and coherent held construction.
The grip is partly hidden by the display hands, and the rendering is more glossy than the original character linework. This is a visual weapon concept, not a fabrication drawing.
The lance has a continuous shaft, separated hand positions and a clearly displayed head.
The head developed a closed oval opening and side scoops instead of the simpler open notch. Subsequent scenes vary its size and contact behavior.
The ivory/dark pistol and blue chamber establish a recognizable fantasy implement with a framed barrel and grip.
Engraving and chamber detail are busier than the simple brief, and A03 shortens the barrel. The image does not establish working internal mechanics.
The repair produces one green axe head, and the later Solene character successfully uses two shaft grips.
The equipment image's near display hand still cups the head/socket rather than wrapping a proper second shaft grip. This repair is partial; use it as an object reference, not a handling reference.
The fox has four grounded paws, a single back shell and tail, with a plausible seam-grazing behavior on a sheltered ledge.
Dark facial detail reduces on a phone; the faceted shell is busier than the smooth-plate brief. Its small role in S01 tests ecology without choosing a mascot.
The heron, dry sill and nest give the flooded district a mundane ecological presence. The high-contrast brush silhouette is distinct from the fox.
The bill is more pointed than the blunt brief, and the far folded wing is naturally hidden. The small scene appearance cannot prove all anatomy.
The repair reduces the shoulder spike forest and preserves the heavy four-legged predator and single tail.
Pointed plates, dark cracks and highlights remain dense, particularly in scenes. The concept suggests pressure hunting, but behavior and encounter balance are provisional.
The tall pale neck, organic legs and huge building scale distinguish the Regent from the squat hound.
Feet became clawed rather than hoof-like, and some plates/crown edges remain pointed. The creature is a scale and threat concept, not a final anatomy sheet.
Riven's low landing/dodge, one falling beam and the visible seam make a new action distinct from the wide crossing scene.
His free hand wraps the blade beyond the guard, and a distinct departure seam is not shown. Handling and the exact teleport mechanism remain unresolved.
Senn and the lowered hound suggest pressure and restraint, with a localized light at the contact area.

The lance contact, folded foreleg and chest compression do not clearly prove added weight; the camera is lower than planned. The ability's cause and limitation rely too much on the accompanying description.

One gun, shoulder mark and existing wall opening make source and target readable. The projected path can plausibly approach in front of the wall and enter the hole; overlap alone does not prove penetration.
The pistol is shorter, the guard detail is lost and Iria faces away. The effect resembles a continuous energy aim more than a clearly demonstrated spirit-pursuing follow-up shot.
Dax's right gauntlet contacts the floor and one narrow ground discharge reaches a separate small barrier. Source, path and consequence are comparatively clear.
This is an early upgrade study, not a second simultaneous power tier or approved canon. Dark armor detail still reduces at phone size.
